question.problem: Consider the portion of the surface $z=y{e}^{x}$ whose projection onto the $xy$-plane is bounded by the lines $y=2x,$ $x=1,$ and the $x$-axis. Find a repeated integral expression for the surface area of this surface.
question.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ defined by $z=f(x,y)$ with $(x,y)\in D,$ the surface area of $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}\sqrt{1+{(\frac{∂z}{∂x})}^{2}+{(\frac{∂z}{∂y})}^{2}}\,\text{d}A.
$$

In this case, our surface is given by

$$
z=y{e}^{x},\,(x,y)\in D
$$

where the region $D$ is given by

$$
D=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,0\le y\le 2x\},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14221663/assets/903b7f3c6bd9721a974160487ca5099fdf54ce02b61697a7830bb662b26d8953.png)

Now, since

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂z}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(y{e}^{x})=y{e}^{x}, \\ \frac{∂z}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(y{e}^{x})={e}^{x},\end{aligned}
$$

the surface area is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}\sqrt{1+{(\frac{∂z}{∂x})}^{2}+{(\frac{∂z}{∂y})}^{2}}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\sqrt{1+(y{e}^{x})^{2}+({e}^{x})^{2}}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\sqrt{1+({y}^{2}+1){e}^{2x}}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2x}\sqrt{1+({y}^{2}+1){e}^{2x}}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$
